concept_options.title: Your Drink Server Is Rescue Crew
concept_options.hook: That flight attendant holding a coffee pot? Trained to fight a cabin fire.
concept_options.visual_approach: A bespoke vertical paper cut-out collage in which familiar service props physically transform into safety equipment: coffee pot to extinguisher, welcome mat to passenger scan, cabin aisle to a 90-second evacuation clock, and aircraft door to a pay clock.
concept_options.target_audience: General travelers and all-ages short-form viewers who know the visible service role but not the regulated safety role.
key_points: Flight attendants are safety crew first, with weeks of evacuation, firefighting, and medical training.
The 90-second rule is a simulated aircraft certification standard, not a promise for every real accident.
The boarding greeting doubles as an early safety and assistance check.
Traditional block-time pay often begins when the aircraft door closes, although newer contracts increasingly add boarding pay.
concept_options.core_message: The calm service role passengers see is the surface of a rigorously trained safety job.
concept_options.cta: Next episode: why your tray table matters more than you think.
concept_options.tone: Friendly, comic, precise, and suitable for all ages.
grounded_in: 14 CFR 121.575 and 121.585 boarding and exit-row rules
Government of Canada block-time pay review and 2026 boarding-pay caveat
concept_options.why_this_works: It turns the audience's most familiar image of the job into a sequence of concrete visual reversals, letting every sourced fact land as a comic paper-object transformation rather than a lecture.

concept_options.title: The Smile Is a Scanner
concept_options.hook: That hello at the aircraft door is doing more work than it looks.
concept_options.visual_approach: Follow one passenger through boarding while a soft paper spotlight reveals the crew's safety checks, then widen into training, evacuation, and pay-clock context.
concept_options.target_audience: Frequent flyers curious about hidden routines.
key_points: The door greeting can reveal intoxication, illness, distress, and need for assistance.
Exit-row suitability is a formal safety concern.
The same crew member trains for evacuation, fire, and first aid.
concept_options.core_message: Hospitality and safety happen at the same time.
concept_options.cta: Next episode: the tiny cabin rules with very big reasons.
concept_options.tone: Warm observational comedy with a gentle mystery reveal.
concept_options.why_this_works: It makes an ordinary human interaction newly legible, but it is narrower than the selected concept and needs more exposition to cover the full brief.

concept_options.title: Ninety Seconds Changes the Job
concept_options.hook: An airliner certification test gives everyone just 90 seconds to get out.
concept_options.visual_approach: Build a paper aircraft cabin around a large tactile countdown, intercutting training drills and passenger behavior as the timer advances.
concept_options.target_audience: Viewers drawn to surprising engineering and safety facts.
key_points: Aircraft over 44 seats face a 90-second simulated evacuation demonstration standard.
Crew training includes exits, slides, firefighting, and protective breathing equipment.
The standard explains why calm cabin procedures matter.
concept_options.core_message: The job is designed around getting a cabin from normal to safe under extreme time pressure.
concept_options.cta: Next episode: why the safety demo sounds so specific.
concept_options.tone: Energetic and factual with a playful countdown.
concept_options.why_this_works: The number is memorable and highly visual, but precision demands that the video clearly identify it as a certification and demonstration standard rather than a real-accident guarantee.

selected_concept.rationale: It best fulfills the brief's promise to explain the whole misunderstood job while providing a cold-open reversal, three-act structure, comic transformations, and room for every required fact.
modifications: Use the 90-second certification fact as the act-two hero moment.
State the boarding-pay caveat so the pay-clock claim remains current and accurate.
End with a next-episode setup about the hidden reasons behind tiny cabin rules.

reuse_strategy.layout_system: One dominant cut-paper subject per beat, alternating centered hero, split-panel comparison, overhead diagram, and intimate character close-up compositions.
reuse_strategy.transition_family: Physical paper actions only: peel, slide, flip, rip reveal, object morph, and brief stop-motion replacement cuts.
reuse_strategy.typography_hierarchy: Chunky hand-cut display labels for hooks and numbers; clean rounded sans-serif captions in two-to-five-word word-level clusters.

stages.approach: Write a 155-175 word, three-act narration with a five-second cold open, title card, sourced caveats, concrete performance cues, and a next-episode closing line.
Map nine visually distinct paper-collage scenes to exact narration windows and caption beats; reserve the signature 90-second paper timer for the single act-two hero moment.

tools.role: Generate one calm, warm female narration track.
tools.why_this_provider: The configured Chirp 3 HD Aoede voice directly matches the requested warm female narration and supports SSML pacing.

tools.role: Find and download a light, playful instrumental background track with commercial-use licensing.
tools.why_this_provider: It is configured, requires no paid generation, and preserves most of the hard budget for contingency.

tools.role: Create all textured paper shapes, characters, props, shadows, and stop-motion motion locally as bespoke SVG/CSS/React artwork.
tools.why_this_provider: Programmatic collage gives exact style consistency across every scene and avoids spending on inconsistent image generations.

stages.approach: Generate narration once, source one free music track, hand-author the paper-collage artwork locally, and render one representative still per scene for the assets gate.
stages.fallback_if_unavailable: If music search fails, use configured Google music generation only after logging the new paid-provider decision; do not change the narration provider or runtime silently.

stages.approach: Lock scene timings to narration, word-level caption clusters, paper-replacement transitions, music ducking, and -14 LUFS delivery.

tools.role: Render the bespoke vertical composition with Remotion.
tools.why_this_provider: Remotion is installed, supports deterministic bespoke animation and word-level captions, and renders locally.

tools.role: Duck music below narration and normalize the final mix.
tools.why_this_provider: Local, deterministic, and integrated with the pipeline.

stages.approach: Render a 1080x1920 H.264 MP4 at 30 fps, mix narration and music, visually inspect extracted keyframes, and verify duration, audio, and encoding with ffprobe.
Create a local YouTube Shorts package containing the final MP4, title, description, sourced-fact notes, and thumbnail frame.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Bespoke local collage artwork versus multiple AI image generations
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: Higher continuity and exact motion control, with more authoring time but near-zero provider spend.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Free licensed music search versus paid music generation
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Use Pixabay music unless search quality fails.
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: Less exact musical tailoring, but reliable production value and no provider cost.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Remotion versus unavailable HyperFrames versus FFmpeg-only composition
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: Remotion supplies deterministic animation and word-level caption support; FFmpeg-only would visibly downgrade the promised motion treatment.

alternative_paths.description: Selected path: bespoke local paper collage, Google TTS, free Pixabay music, Remotion atelier render.
alternative_paths.what_changes: No change; this maximizes consistency while staying far below budget.

alternative_paths.description: Generate a set of paper-collage background plates with Google Imagen and animate them in Remotion.
alternative_paths.what_changes: Faster authoring but weaker character and texture consistency across scenes.

alternative_paths.description: FFmpeg-only still-led cut with local vector art.
alternative_paths.what_changes: Would lose bespoke scene animation and word-level caption motion; rejected because it breaks the delivery promise.

production_plan.art_direction: A one-off tactile safety-manual storybook: muted teal, sky, cream, and charcoal paper with coral-orange reserved for danger, countdowns, and key reveals; rough torn edges, soft dimensional shadows, tiny registration jitter, and object-to-object paper replacement morphs.

taste_profile.design_read: The piece should feel like a friendly children's safety book assembled on an animation table, while its factual precision earns adult trust. Comedy comes from literal paper-object transformations, not from mocking passengers or crew.
taste_profile.palette_discipline: Muted cream, dusty teal, faded sky blue, charcoal, and kraft tan; coral-orange is the single warm accent and appears only on safety-critical objects and numbers.
taste_profile.layout_variation: Alternate close character portraits, wide cabin tableaux, overhead diagrams, split comparisons, and one full-frame typographic countdown; never repeat the same primary subject in adjacent scenes.
taste_profile.reference_strategy: Use physical cut-paper construction cues and stop-motion timing as principles, with no reference-copying or stock component reuse.
anti_patterns: more than one warm accent color
quality_gates: Every scene visibly reads as textured paper at 1080x1920.
The first spoken reversal lands within five seconds.
The 90-second statement visibly includes certification context.
Captions are legible in two-to-five-word clusters and stay clear of YouTube UI zones.
No two adjacent scenes share the same primary visual subject or layout.

music_source.mood_direction: Light plucked percussion and warm marimba or pizzicato, 100-115 BPM, playful but not childish, no vocals, no dramatic trailer hits.

voice_selection.rationale: Configured warm female voice with the calm clarity needed for all-ages factual narration.
voice_selection.delivery_style: Calm, warm, lightly amused, never breathless; confident on safety facts and gently conspiratorial on the boarding and pay reveals.
voice_selection.pacing_policy: About 145-155 words per minute, with micro-pauses after visual reversals and a full beat before the 90-second reveal.

line_items.operation: One approximately 165-word Chirp 3 HD narration generation
line_items.notes: Conservative allowance; actual billing may be lower or covered by quota.
